open_points.subject: A15 rule 1 — record-store refusal condition
open_points.text: a function execution whose record the store refused writes none
open_points.question: Exactly which store outcomes count as the store refusing the record and trigger a kernel stop and re-execution?
options: Only the specific failure defined by A03 rule 7
Any failure while inserting the NodeExecution
Only failures known to leave the entire store transaction unchanged
open_points.default_guess: Apply this only to the atomic NodeExecution-write failure covered by A03 rule 7, provided the transaction left no durable change.

witness.initial: A function element finishes execution and the attempted NodeExecution insert is rejected by a store constraint or fails during commit.
events: The kernel attempts to persist the NodeExecution.
The store does not accept the record.
outcomes: Every rejected insert is treated as the stated refusal: the kernel stops and startup recovery executes the function again.
Only the A03 rule 7 failure class triggers that behavior; another rejected insert is handled as an ordinary store error.
witness.observer: The caller and the operator restarting the kernel

open_points.subject: A15 rule 1 and A04 admission executions
open_points.text: a function execution whose record the store refused writes none: the kernel stops and recovery executes it again
open_points.question: Does “a function execution” here mean only a run element whose record is a NodeExecution, or also a trial/admission execution whose record is a TrialExecution?
options: Only real run elements and NodeExecution records
Every sandboxed function execution, including try and admission TrialExecutions
open_points.default_guess: Limit the exception to run elements and NodeExecution records because A15 rule 1 otherwise discusses NodeExecution traces.

witness.initial: Admission is running an implementation on a trial case.
events: The store refuses its TrialExecution record.
outcomes: The exception applies, so the kernel stops and recovery repeats that trial execution.
The exception does not apply because no NodeExecution was being written; admission follows separate store-failure behavior.
witness.observer: The submitting agent and the admission evidence reader

open_points.subject: A13 rule 3, A15 rule 1, and the carried attempt-number rule
open_points.text: a position being the run, node, `map_index`, attempt number, port and list index, which only a retry of the same attempt number writes again, after a restart left that attempt without a record
open_points.question: When a function execution leaves no NodeExecution because its record was refused, did that execution take an attempt number, and what attempt number and spool position must recovery use?
options: The failed-to-record execution took the pending ordinal and recovery reuses that same attempt number and position
The failed-to-record execution took no number; recovery receives the next NodeExecution ordinal, while abandoned output uses an unnumbered temporary position
open_points.default_guess: Treat the failed-to-record execution as taking no number semantically; recovery's eventual record receives the next stored ordinal, while temporary artifacts use that pending ordinal only as an internal replaceable position.

witness.initial: A function element has no stored NodeExecution, and its next stored record would have attempt_number 1.
events: The function executes and writes a file to the run spool.
The store refuses its NodeExecution record.
The kernel restarts and recovery executes the function again.
outcomes: Under A13 rule 3, both physical executions write the position carrying attempt number 1, and the retry replaces the first file.
Under the carried rule, the first execution takes no attempt number, so its file cannot have the M22 position whose identity includes attempt_number; only the recovered execution can take number 1.
witness.observer: The spool/store implementation and anyone inspecting SpooledFile facts after recovery

open_points.subject: A15 formal invariant for NodeExecution cardinality
open_points.question: Does an execution whose NodeExecution write was refused count as a concluded attempt, and if so how must the invariant express the new no-record exception?
options: It is a concluded attempt, so the invariant must exclude record-write refusal explicitly
It is not a concluded attempt because element conclusion exists only through a stored NodeExecution
open_points.default_guess: Define it as an execution that did not become a concluded attempt, and rewrite the invariant to state that distinction explicitly.

witness.initial: A function finishes successfully but the store refuses its NodeExecution record.
events: The NodeExecution insert is refused and the kernel stops.
outcomes: The normative rule requires zero NodeExecutions for that execution.
The formal invariant, if the finished execution is a concluded attempt, requires exactly one NodeExecution.
witness.observer: The invariant checker and the trace reader

open_points.subject: A15 changed record-refusal behavior
open_points.text: a function execution whose record the store refused writes none: the kernel stops and recovery executes it again (K-09, A03 rule 7)
open_points.question: What Required tests item must show the no-record exception, the kernel stop, and exactly one recovery re-execution?
options: Add a test that refuses the first NodeExecution write, proves no record was left, restarts, and proves the function executes again and its successful record is stored once
Extend Required test 6 with the store-refusal and recovery history
open_points.default_guess: Add a separate Required tests item covering refusal, absence of the first record, restart, one re-execution, and the resulting stored record.
